content.value_statement: Choosing tests and reporting results correctly requires careful assumptions, diagnostics, and interpretation. This skill provides structured guidance, Python examples, automated checks, and APA-style reporting templates.
actual_capabilities: Select t-tests, ANOVA, chi-square tests, correlations, regressions, and nonparametric alternatives from study design and variable types.
Check normality, variance homogeneity, linearity, and outliers with the included Python module and diagnostic plots.
Calculate and interpret effect sizes, confidence intervals, sample sizes, and sensitivity analyses.
Guide Bayesian t-tests, regression, prior selection, convergence checks, posterior summaries, and Bayes factors.
Produce APA-style result structures for common frequentist and Bayesian analyses.
Recommend remedies when assumptions fail, including robust, transformed, or nonparametric approaches.
limitations: Statistical recommendations depend on accurate variable definitions, study design, and sampling information.
The included automation focuses on assumption checks and does not execute every analysis described in the references.
Python examples require compatible third-party packages and may need adaptation for local data structures.
Outputs require expert review for causal claims, regulated decisions, and complex study designs.

use_cases.title: Plan Academic Research
use_cases.description: Plan a preregistered experiment, determine sample size, check assumptions, and prepare complete results for a manuscript.

use_cases.title: Diagnose Business Models
use_cases.description: Choose and diagnose models for observational data while separating statistical significance from practical importance.

use_cases.title: Learn Test Selection
use_cases.description: Learn why a test fits a research question and practice interpreting effect sizes, intervals, and diagnostics.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Statistical Test
prompt_templates.prompt: I have [outcome type], [predictor or groups], and [study design]. Recommend a statistical test and explain its required assumptions.

prompt_templates.title: Build an Assumption Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess assumptions for [test] using these variables: [details]. Provide checks, decision thresholds, remedies, and a concise reporting plan.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze and Report Results
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze [dataset description] for [research question] using [preferred language]. Include diagnostics, effect sizes, confidence intervals, and an APA-style interpretation.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Advanced Strategies
prompt_templates.prompt: Design frequentist and Bayesian analyses for [question]. Compare priors, power, multiplicity controls, diagnostics, sensitivity analyses, and reporting requirements.

output_examples.input: Two independent groups have continuous scores and unequal variances. Which test should I use?
output_examples.output: Use Welch's independent t-test if observations are independent. Check distributions and outliers, then report group summaries, the test statistic, interval, and effect size.

output_examples.input: A Shapiro-Wilk test is significant for one of three treatment groups. What should I do?
output_examples.output: Inspect the Q-Q plot and outliers before changing methods. Compare a robust or nonparametric analysis and report whether conclusions remain stable.

output_examples.input: Summarize a significant two-group comparison in APA style.
output_examples.output: Condition A scores exceeded Condition B scores, Welch t(91.4) = 2.87, p = .005, with Cohen's d = 0.59 and a 95% confidence interval.

best_practices: Define hypotheses, variables, and the analysis plan before examining outcomes.
Check assumptions and diagnostics before interpreting estimates or significance tests.
Report effect sizes, uncertainty intervals, all planned analyses, and transparent sensitivity checks.
anti_patterns: Do not select tests only because they produce smaller p-values.
Do not remove outliers without investigating their source and reporting the decision.
Do not treat statistical significance as proof of practical importance or causation.

faq.question: What data formats can I use?
faq.answer: The guidance works with tabular data, arrays, or summary statistics when the prompt clearly defines variables and groups.

faq.question: Does the skill run analysis code?
faq.answer: It can draft and explain Python analysis code. Execution depends on the host tool, installed packages, and dataset access.

faq.question: Which assumptions can the included module check?
faq.answer: It checks normality, variance homogeneity, linearity, and outliers, with diagnostic plots and practical recommendations.

faq.question: Does it support Bayesian analysis?
faq.answer: Yes. The references cover priors, Bayes factors, credible intervals, convergence diagnostics, posterior checks, and common Bayesian models.

faq.question: Can it prepare publication-ready results?
faq.answer: It provides APA-style structures, reporting elements, and examples. Final tables, figures, and wording still require author review.

faq.question: Can it replace a statistical consultant?
faq.answer: No. Expert review remains important for complex designs, causal inference, regulated decisions, and analyses with serious real-world consequences.
